description: Extract of APK Builder 0.4.0 environment.json (profile cpp-native-v1): the native-prebuilt rules and SDK limits only. Device and installation details are deliberately left out. Used by scripts/verify_elf.py.

native_prebuilt.status: IMPLEMENTED - DESKTOP VALIDATED; PHONE VALIDATION PENDING
native_prebuilt.status_meaning: Implemented in Build 004 and validated on a desktop: 24 real ARM64 test libraries, hostile inputs and three complete test apps were built, signed and independently verified. No APK built this way has been installed or run on a phone yet, and no real llama.cpp library has been packaged or loaded. Treat every phone result as untested until the owner reports it.
native_prebuilt.opt_in: Add the object native.prebuilt to apkbuilder.json (profile cpp-native-v1 only). Without it this extension does not exist: any .so file in a project is rejected exactly as in Build 003.
native_prebuilt.what_it_does: Copies the declared ARM64 shared libraries into the APK byte for byte (lib/arm64-v8a/, stored uncompressed on 16 KiB boundaries) after checking each one as data. APK Builder never loads or executes them. They run only inside the built app.

layout.jniLibs/arm64-v8a/lib<name>.so: the prebuilt libraries: only this folder, only files named lib<name>.so (letters, digits, . _ -), no sub-folders, no other ABI
layout.jni/**: optional in this mode: C/C++ sources of a JNI bridge that APK Builder compiles and links against the prebuilt libraries; headers of the prebuilt libraries belong here too
layout.src/**/*.java: required as always: the Java side that calls System.loadLibrary

libraries.sha256: <optional: 64 lower-case hex characters; if present the file must match>
libraries.origin: <where the binary comes from, e.g. the release URL and asset name>

modes: Source bridge + prebuilt engine: jni/ holds a small C or C++ bridge with the JNI functions; native.library_name names it; it is linked against every declared prebuilt library that it actually uses. Java loads only the bridge.

Prebuilt bridge (+ prebuilt engine): no jni/ sources and no native.library_name; one of the prebuilt libraries exports the JNI functions (Java_<package>_<Class>_<method> or JNI_OnLoad). Java loads that library.
An engine library alone is rejected (PREBUILT_NO_JNI_ENTRY): a library such as libllama.so has a C API, not JNI functions. It always needs a bridge, compiled here or prebuilt.
rules: Every .so file under jniLibs/arm64-v8a/ must be listed in native.prebuilt.libraries, and every listed file must be in the ZIP. Nothing is packaged that is not declared.

Each entry states file, origin, version and license. They are recorded next to the SHA-256 that APK Builder measures; APK Builder does not verify them. sha256 is optional: when given, the file must match it.
A library's file name must equal its SONAME. Dependencies (DT_NEEDED) are found by SONAME, so do not rename library files.

Everything a library needs must be: another declared library, libc++_shared.so, or a public Android system library from allowed_system_libraries. Include every companion library of an engine; APK Builder names the missing one.
libc++_shared.so is owned by APK Builder. A project cannot supply it. When any packaged library needs it, or the project has C++ sources, the pinned copy bundled with the builder is added.

Load order: Java calls System.loadLibrary once, for the library that has the JNI functions. Android (API 23+) loads its dependencies from the APK by itself, dependencies first; build results list that order as load_order.
A library built for a newer Android API level than the project's min_sdk fails with UNSUPPORTED_MIN_SDK; raise build.min_sdk (a repair JSON with set_min_sdk can do it).
Write the Java side so that a failed load is shown, not fatal: catch Throwable around System.loadLibrary and display it. Run native work on a background thread and give it a way to be cancelled.
Models and other large data files do not belong in the project ZIP. Let the app's user pick them at run time.
library_requirements: ELF64, little-endian, AArch64 (arm64-v8a), a shared object (not an executable, not a .o or .a file)
every load segment aligned to 16384 bytes or more, no two load segments in one 16 KiB page, GNU_RELRO not sharing its last 16 KiB page with writable data (link with -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384)
a SONAME equal to the file name; DT_NEEDED entries that are plain library names, never paths
section headers present and consistent with the dynamic segment; a DT_HASH or DT_GNU_HASH table; no text relocations; no segment that is both writable and executable

allowed_system_libraries.meaning: public Android (NDK) libraries a prebuilt library may need, with the Android API level from which each exists

limits.note: Only the per-file limit differs for a prebuilt library; the limits on the whole ZIP are the Build 003 limits, so a project cannot demand more memory or storage than before.

failure_codes.PREBUILT_UNDECLARED_FILE: a .so file is under jniLibs/arm64-v8a/ but not listed in native.prebuilt.libraries
failure_codes.PREBUILT_MISSING_FILE: a library is listed in native.prebuilt.libraries but the file is not in the ZIP
failure_codes.PREBUILT_HASH_MISMATCH: the file's SHA-256 differs from the sha256 pinned in apkbuilder.json
failure_codes.PREBUILT_ELF_INVALID: the file is not a readable ELF library (truncated, malformed, empty, not ELF at all)
failure_codes.PREBUILT_WRONG_ABI: the library is not 64-bit little-endian AArch64 (for example armeabi-v7a, x86 or x86_64)
failure_codes.PREBUILT_NOT_SHARED_OBJECT: the file is an executable program or an object file, not a shared library
failure_codes.PREBUILT_NOT_16K_COMPATIBLE: the library is not linked for 16 KiB memory pages (load segments, shared pages or GNU_RELRO)
failure_codes.PREBUILT_LOADER_INCOMPATIBLE: Android's dynamic linker would refuse the library (text relocations, a writable and executable segment, missing or inconsistent section headers, no symbol hash table)
failure_codes.PREBUILT_SONAME_MISMATCH: the library has no SONAME, or its SONAME is not its file name
failure_codes.PREBUILT_RESERVED_NAME: the file uses the name of an Android system library
failure_codes.PREBUILT_DUPLICATE_LIBRARY: the file has the same name as the library compiled from this project's jni/ sources
failure_codes.PREBUILT_DEPENDENCY_INVALID: a DT_NEEDED entry is a path or is unreadable
failure_codes.PREBUILT_DEPENDENCY_MISSING: the library needs another library that is neither declared in the project nor a public Android system library
failure_codes.PREBUILT_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE: the libraries need each other in a circle
failure_codes.PREBUILT_LIBCXX_CONFLICT: the project tries to supply libc++_shared.so, or a library exports its own C++ runtime while libc++_shared.so is also packaged
failure_codes.PREBUILT_LIBCXX_INCOMPATIBLE: a library needs C++ runtime symbols that the bundled, pinned libc++_shared.so does not provide
failure_codes.PREBUILT_NO_JNI_ENTRY: no jni/ sources and no prebuilt library exports a JNI function, so Java could not call into the libraries
failure_codes.PREBUILT_API_LEVEL_TOO_NEW: a library needs a newer Android API level than this builder can target
failure_codes.PREBUILT_TOO_LARGE: one library is larger than the per-library limit
failure_codes.UNSUPPORTED_MIN_SDK: SETTINGS, repairable by JSON (set_min_sdk): the libraries need a newer Android than the project's min_sdk
failure_codes.LOW_MEMORY: DEVICE: not enough free memory to package libraries of this size; nothing in the project is wrong
failure_codes.ZIP_BOMB: ARCHIVE: an entry is larger than the per-file limit (48 MiB for a prebuilt library, 16 MiB for anything else) or the archive exceeds its total limits

native_prebuilt.result_record: A successful build result contains native_prebuilt: each library's name, bytes, SHA-256, declared origin/version/license, SONAME, dependencies and how each was satisfied, load_order, and its position in the APK.
not_supported: libraries that need non-public platform libraries or vendor libraries (for example libOpenCL.so)
prebuilt libraries in any profile other than cpp-native-v1
GPU, Vulkan or NNAPI acceleration has not been evaluated; only CPU libraries are in scope
